name: Fetch and Summarize Weather Data from Public API
prompt:
Fetch current weather data for three cities using the public wttr.in JSON API and save a structured report.

For each city, fetch: https://wttr.in/{city}?format=j1
- Cities: London, Tokyo, Sydney

From each response, extract:
- temp_C (current temperature in Celsius, from current_condition[0].temp_C)
- weatherDesc (description string, from current_condition[0].weatherDesc[0].value)
- humidity (from current_condition[0].humidity)
- windspeedKmph (from current_condition[0].windspeedKmph)

Save to weather_report.json with this exact structure:
{
  "cities": [
    {
      "city": "London",
      "temp_C": <number>,
      "weatherDesc": "<string>",
      "humidity": <number>,
      "windspeedKmph": <number>
    },
    { "city": "Tokyo", ... },
    { "city": "Sydney", ... }
  ],
  "hottest_city": "<city with highest temp_C>",
  "coldest_city": "<city with lowest temp_C>",
  "fetched_count": 3
}

All numeric fields must be actual numbers (not strings). If the API is unavailable, use realistic placeholder values but set a field "data_source": "fallback" at the top level. If API data is used, set "data_source": "live".

Also save a plain text summary to weather_summary.txt with one line per city in the format:
{City}: {temp_C}°C, {weatherDesc}, Humidity: {humidity}%, Wind: {windspeedKmph} km/h

criteria.description: weather_report.json exists in the working directory.
weather_summary.txt exists in the working directory.
weather_report.json cities array contains exactly 3 entries.
City names in the cities array are exactly "London", "Tokyo", and "Sydney".
Each city object has temp_C, weatherDesc, humidity, and windspeedKmph fields.
temp_C, humidity, and windspeedKmph are all numeric types (not strings) for each city.
criteria.testPattern: temp_C is a number for each city|humidity and windspeedKmph are numbers

criteria.description: hottest_city and coldest_city are valid city names that match the entries with the highest and lowest temp_C respectively.
weather_summary.txt has exactly 3 non-empty lines, each containing a °C symbol and wind/km/h information.
criteria.testPattern: has exactly 3 non-empty lines|each line contains city name, temperature symbol, and wind speed info

criteria.description: data_source field is present and equals either "live" or "fallback".

eval.rubric:
Context: The agent fetched weather data and produced a structured report.

Criterion 1: Data Completeness (Weight: 60%)
1.0: All three cities are present with all four required fields (temp_C, weatherDesc, humidity, windspeedKmph) as correct types, hottest_city and coldest_city are correctly identified, fetched_count is 3.
0.5: All cities present but one field is missing or incorrectly typed for one city.
0: One or more cities are missing entirely.

Criterion 2: Summary File Quality (Weight: 40%)
1.0: weather_summary.txt has exactly 3 lines, each following the specified format with city name, temperature, description, humidity percentage, and wind speed.
0.5: Summary exists but format deviates from spec for some lines.
0: Summary file is missing.
eval.name: Quality Judge
